questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: P is the mother of R's wife Q, so P is R's mother-in-law.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: X and Y are siblings and Y is Z's daughter, so X is Z's son.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: M is the son of O's sister N, so M is O's nephew.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Amit is the husband of Sunita. Sunita is the daughter of Ramesh. How is Amit related to Ramesh?
questions.e: Amit married Ramesh's daughter, so Amit is Ramesh's son-in-law.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.e: K is L's wife and L is N's father, so K is N's mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is B's sister. B is C's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.e: A is the sister of D's wife B, so A is D's sister-in-law.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ravi's mother's only son's daughter is Suman. How is Ravi related to Suman?
questions.e: Ravi's mother's only son is Ravi himself; his daughter is Suman, so Ravi is Suman's father.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pooja is the niece of Rahul. Rahul is the only brother of Pooja's mother. How is Rahul related to Pooja?
questions.e: Rahul is the brother of Pooja's mother, so he is Pooja's uncle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A man points to a photo and says: 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is she related to him?
questions.e: Grandfather's only son is his father; the father's daughter is his sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: T is the father of U. U is the brother of V. V is the mother of W. How is T related to W?
questions.e: T is the father of W's mother V, so T is W's grandfather.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: The company has decided to open 50 new branches in rural areas next year.
The company expects rural banking to be profitable.
Assumption II: Competitors have no rural branches.
questions.e: A company expands only if it expects the move to pay off; nothing is said about competitors.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: The school made attendance below 75% a bar on appearing for final exams.
Low attendance hurts academic performance.
Assumption II: Parents support the rule.
questions.e: The rule only makes sense if the school believes attendance affects performance; II is unstated.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: Prices of onions have risen sharply due to crop damage from floods.
The government should release buffer stocks to cool prices.
Course of action II: The government should ban all onion exports permanently.
questions.e: Releasing buffer stock targets the price rise; banning exports is a bigger, unasked step here.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: Many employees are resigning because of long working hours.
The company should introduce flexible working hours.
Course of action II: The company should cut salaries to reduce costs.
questions.e: Flexible hours address the cause; cutting salaries would worsen attrition.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: 'Study regularly and you will clear the bank exam,' said the mentor.
Regular study leads to success in the exam.
Assumption II: Only coaching institutes produce toppers.
questions.e: The advice rests on regularity helping; II about coaching is not assumed.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: The municipal corporation will repair all roads before the monsoon.
Roads are currently in bad shape.
Assumption II: The corporation has unlimited funds.
questions.e: Ordering repairs assumes repairs are needed; II about funds is unstated.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: Smoking in public places is punishable by a fine of ₹500.
The fine will deter people from smoking in public.
Assumption II: Smoking will be banned everywhere soon.
questions.e: Penalties are imposed on the belief they deter; II about a total ban is not assumed.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: The bank reported a 20% rise in digital transactions this quarter.
Customers are shifting to digital banking.
Conclusion II: The bank will close all physical branches.
questions.e: The data supports a digital shift; it says nothing about branches closing.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: All candidates must carry a valid photo ID to the exam centre.
Candidates without ID may be denied entry.
Conclusion II: Only Aadhaar cards will be accepted.
questions.e: A mandatory ID rule implies denial without it; II about Aadhaar-only is too specific.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Statement: The team won the match because of excellent fielding.
Fielding was the decisive factor in the win.
Assumption II: The team's batting was poor.
questions.e: Crediting the win to fielding assumes it was decisive; II about batting is unstated.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
What is the value of x?
I. 2x + 6 = 18.
II. x is a positive integer.
questions.e: From I: 2x = 12 → x = 6. I alone suffices.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Is A taller than B?
I. A is taller than C.
II. C is taller than B.
questions.e: Only together do I and II give A > C > B, so A is taller than B.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
What is the code for 'bank'?
I. 'bank exam' is coded as 'ti na'.
II. 'exam hall' is coded as 'na mo'.
questions.e: Together: 'exam' = na, so 'bank' = ti. Neither alone separates the words.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
How many students are in the class?
I. Girls are 40% of the class.
II. There are 18 boys.
questions.e: Boys = 60% = 18 → total 30. Both needed.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
Is x > 5?

II. x < 10.
questions.e: x could be 4 or 7 — neither statement settles whether x > 5.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q:
What is the area of the rectangle?
I. Its length is 12 cm.
II. Its diagonal is 13 cm.
questions.e: Breadth = √(13²−12²) = 5, area = 60. Both needed.

questions.q:

I. P is taller than Q.
II. R is shorter than Q.
questions.e: I gives P > Q and II gives Q > R, but each alone... recompute: I alone insufficient. Fix.

questions.subject: English

questions.subject: English

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) The data/(B) was analysed/(C) carefully by the team./(D) No error.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) Scarcely had he/(B) finished his lunch/(C) than the phone rang./(D) No error.
questions.e: 'Scarcely…when', not 'than': 'Scarcely had he finished…when the phone rang'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) She asked me/(B) that where I/(C) had kept the keys./(D) No error.
questions.e: No 'that' with a wh-question in indirect speech: 'asked me where I had kept'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) The thief was/(B) caught red-handed/(C) by the police yesterday./(D) No error.
questions.e: The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) He has/(B) many works/(C) to finish today./(D) No error.
questions.e: 'Work' is uncountable: 'much work'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) Between you and I,/(B) this plan/(C) will not succeed./(D) No error.
questions.e: After a preposition use the objective case: 'Between you and me'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) The reason/(B) of his failure/(C) was his laziness./(D) No error.
questions.e: Idiom is 'the reason for his failure'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) I have known him/(B) since a long time/(C) now./(D) No error.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) The news/(B) are shocking/(C) to everyone./(D) No error.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) She can/(B) be able to/(C) solve this problem./(D) No error.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: (A) One must/(B) do his duty/(C) sincerely./(D) No error.

questions.subject: English

questions.e: Small Finance Banks carry a higher 75% priority sector lending target, reflecting their financial-inclusion mandate.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The maximum balance a payments bank can hold per customer was raised in 2021 to:
questions.e: The RBI doubled the per-customer end-of-day balance limit for payments banks from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh in 2021.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: India's first payments bank to begin operations, in November 2016, was:
questions.e: Airtel Payments Bank launched in November 2016 as India's first payments bank; India Post Payments Bank followed on September 1, 2018.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The retail CBDC pilot (e₹-R) was launched by the RBI in which month?
questions.e: The wholesale CBDC pilot began October 31, 2022 and the retail e₹ pilot launched on December 1, 2022.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: NEFT became available 24x7 from which date?
questions.e: NEFT went 24x7 on December 16, 2019; RTGS followed with round-the-clock availability on December 14, 2020.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Cheque Truncation System in India operates on the CTS-2010 standard. Cheques are cleared on the basis of:
questions.e: CTS-2010 clears cheques using electronic images and MICR-line data instead of physically moving the paper instrument.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Marginal Standing Facility was introduced by the RBI in which year?
questions.e: MSF was introduced in May 2011, letting banks borrow overnight against approved securities at a penal rate above the repo rate.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Standing Deposit Facility, an overnight deposit window without collateral, was introduced in:
questions.e: SDF was introduced in April 2022 as the floor of the LAF corridor, replacing the fixed-rate reverse repo as the operating target anchor.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility, the RBI's main monetary policy operating framework, was introduced following which committee's recommendation?
questions.e: LAF was introduced in June 2000 on the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee on Banking Sector Reforms (1998).

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: SARFAESI Act, which lets banks enforce security interest without court intervention, was enacted in:
questions.e: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act was passed in 2002.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 mandates completion of the corporate insolvency resolution process within:
questions.e: IBC requires CIRP completion within 330 days including extensions and litigation time, after the 2019 amendment.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, merging the banking, NBFC and digital-transaction ombudsman schemes, was launched in:
questions.e: The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme was launched in November 2021 with the 'One Nation One Ombudsman' approach.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Regional Rural Banks were established under which legislation?
questions.e: RRBs were set up under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, with the first five RRBs inaugurated on October 2, 1975.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.e: NABARD was created on the recommendation of the Sivaraman Committee (1979) to refinance agriculture and rural development.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Lead Bank Scheme, assigning a lead bank to each district, was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of:
questions.e: The Gadgil Study Group's recommendation led to the Lead Bank Scheme in December 1969 for district-level credit planning.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The second round of bank nationalisation in 1980 covered how many banks?
questions.e: Six banks with deposits above Rs. 200 crore were nationalised in April 1980, after 14 banks in July 1969.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The mega-merger of 10 public sector banks into 4 became effective on:
questions.e: The amalgamation of 10 PSBs into 4 (PNB, Canara, Union Bank, Indian Bank as anchors) took effect on April 1, 2020.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Allahabad Bank, founded in 1865 as India's oldest joint-stock bank, was merged into which bank in 2020?
questions.e: Allahabad Bank amalgamated with Indian Bank effective April 1, 2020.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The headquarters of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) is at:
questions.e: IFSCA, established in 2020, is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India's first IFSC.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A bank's Cash Reserve Ratio is maintained with the RBI in the form of:
questions.e: CRR is the share of net demand and time liabilities banks must hold as cash balances with the RBI; it earns no interest.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Which of the following earns interest for banks?
questions.e: SLR is held in interest-earning assets like government securities, while CRR balances with the RBI earn no interest.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: When the RBI wants to absorb durable liquidity from the banking system, it typically:
o: Buys dollars in the spot market
questions.e: Open market sales of government securities drain rupee liquidity from the system; purchases inject it.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A borrower who has defaulted on a term loan for 95 days is classified as:
questions.e: An account turns NPA only after 90 days overdue; at 95 days past due it is typically in the SMA-2 special-mention category but still standard.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: An NPA that has remained in the substandard category for 12 months is reclassified as:
questions.e: Substandard assets are NPAs up to 12 months; beyond 12 months they become doubtful assets with higher provisioning.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Under the IBC, the Committee of Creditors approves a resolution plan with what minimum voting share?
questions.e: CoC approval requires at least 66% of voting share of financial creditors; several other decisions need 51%.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: In a letter of credit transaction, the issuing bank's undertaking is primarily towards:
questions.e: The issuing bank undertakes to pay the beneficiary (exporter) against compliant documents, independent of the underlying sales contract.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Nostro and Vostro accounts are used in:
questions.e: A Nostro account is a domestic bank's account held abroad in foreign currency; from the foreign bank's view it is a Vostro account.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The UFBU's three-day nationwide bank strike of 28–30 September 2026 was called mainly to press which demand?
o: A five-day banking week with all Saturdays as holidays
questions.e: UFBU's central demand is a five-day banking week (all Saturdays as holidays). A conciliation meeting before the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner remained inconclusive, so the strike went ahead.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Ahead of the 28–30 September 2026 bank strike, the RBI approved which of the following for Sunday, 27 September 2026?
o: Normal functioning of all branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests
A bank holiday in metro cities only
questions.e: The RBI approved keeping all bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests fully operational on Sunday, 27 September 2026, so PSBs and RRBs functioned normally that day.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The three-day bank strike beginning 28 September 2026 followed which earlier strike action in the same month?
questions.e: A one-day nationwide bank strike on 11 September 2026 failed to resolve the unions' key demands, leading UFBU to escalate to the three-day strike of 28–30 September.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: During the 28–30 September 2026 bank strike, which services were generally expected to remain available?
o: UPI, mobile banking and internet banking
questions.e: Digital channels — UPI, mobile banking and internet banking — generally keep working during branch strikes; SBI issued an advisory to customers ahead of the strike.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: As of late September 2026, markets expected the RBI to take which repo-rate action at its October 2026 policy?
questions.e: Reports in late September 2026 expected the RBI to raise the repo rate to 5.50% in October as inflation broadened; HSBC projected a 50-bp hike across FY27.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Why did the government/RBI arrange normal banking on Sunday, 27 September 2026?
o: To prevent a five-day disruption of services from 26–30 September
To launch a new currency series
To conduct the RBI's annual audit
questions.e: With the 4th Saturday (26 Sep) and Sunday (27 Sep) holidays followed by the 28–30 Sep strike, customers faced five days without branch services; Sunday banking on 27 Sep broke that chain.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Central government employees and pensioners received their September 2026 salary on which date, ahead of the bank strike?
questions.e: September salaries for central government employees and pensioners were credited early, on 25 September 2026, ahead of the 28–30 September strike window.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Under RBI KYC directions, accounts of high-risk customers must undergo periodic review at least once every:
questions.e: Periodic updation of KYC: high-risk customers at least every 2 years, medium-risk every 8 years and low-risk every 10 years.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Central KYC Registry (CKYC) is managed by:
questions.e: CERSAI operates the Central KYC Records Registry, letting customers complete KYC once for use across financial institutions.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: CIBIL, Equifax, Experian and CRIF High Mark are examples of:
questions.e: They are RBI-licensed credit information companies under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A credit score in India is typically reported on a scale of:
questions.e: CIBIL and other bureaus score individuals from 300 to 900; 750+ is generally considered good for loan approvals.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The maximum amount per transaction under IMPS via mobile banking is generally:
questions.e: IMPS allows instant 24x7 transfers up to Rs. 5 lakh per transaction through mobile and internet banking channels.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: RTGS is primarily meant for:
o: High-value transfers of Rs. 2 lakh and above
questions.e: RTGS settles high-value transfers of Rs. 2 lakh and above individually in real time, on a 24x7 basis since December 2020.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Which digital payment mode works on a deferred net settlement basis?
questions.e: NEFT settles in half-hourly batches on a deferred net basis, unlike the real-time gross settlement of RTGS or instant IMPS/UPI.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A 'green deposit' framework issued by the RBI relates to deposits whose proceeds finance:
questions.e: The RBI's 2023 green-deposit framework channels deposit proceeds to green activities like renewable energy and clean transport.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The RBI's framework for 'wilful defaulters' was overhauled in 2024. A wilful defaulter tag requires outstanding of at least:
questions.e: The 2024 master direction applies the wilful-defaulter framework to borrowers with outstanding of Rs. 25 lakh and above.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The '5/25' and 'S4A' schemes of the RBI were designed for:
questions.e: The 5/25 flexible structuring and Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets addressed large stressed loans.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Asset Reconstruction Companies in India require a minimum net owned fund of:
questions.e: The RBI raised the minimum net owned fund for ARCs to Rs. 300 crore in October 2022.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: NARCL, the 'bad bank' for large stressed assets, acquires exposures above what threshold?
questions.e: National Asset Reconstruction Company takes over fully provisioned stressed loans above Rs. 500 crore from banks.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: IDRBT, the RBI's technology research arm for banking, is located in:
questions.e: The Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology is based in Hyderabad.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Bharat Bill Payment System is operated by:
questions.e: NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd., a subsidiary of NPCI, operates the interoperable bill-payment platform.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: TReDS platforms (RXIL, M1xchange, InvoiceMart) primarily serve:
questions.e: Trade Receivables Discounting System platforms let MSMEs auction their trade receivables to financiers for working capital.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The account that NRIs use to deposit income earned in India, like rent, is the:
questions.e: NRO accounts hold income earned in India; NRE holds foreign earnings repatriable freely, and FCNR(B) holds foreign-currency term deposits.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: FCNR(B) deposits are denominated in:
questions.e: Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits are held in designated foreign currencies, shielding depositors from rupee depreciation.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Liberalised Remittance Scheme allows resident individuals to remit up to what amount per financial year?
questions.e: LRS permits resident individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for permitted current and capital account transactions.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: SWIFT, the global financial messaging network, is headquartered in:
questions.e: The Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication is headquartered at La Hulpe, Belgium (Brussels).

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A bank guarantee is best described as:
questions.e: Bank guarantees are non-fund-based, off-balance-sheet commitments that crystallise only if the customer defaults.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The 'bank rate' differs from the repo rate mainly because:
o: It applies to longer-term refinance without collateral resale
It is decided by commercial banks
It applies only to foreign banks
questions.e: The Bank Rate is the rate for RBI's longer-term refinance/MSF-type facilities and also serves as the penal rate reference; repo is for short-term collateralised borrowing.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Ways and Means Advances are short-term advances given by the RBI to:
questions.e: WMA bridges temporary mismatches in government receipts and payments for the Centre and states.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Cash Management Bill is issued by the Government of India to meet:
questions.e: CMBs are short-term instruments (under 91 days) to tide over temporary mismatches in government cash flows.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Treasury bills are issued at a discount and redeemed at par. Which maturities are currently issued in India?
questions.e: The government issues 91-day, 182-day and 364-day T-bills through RBI auctions.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Negotiated Dealing System-Order Matching (NDS-OM) is the RBI's platform for:
o: Secondary market trading in government securities
questions.e: NDS-OM is the electronic order-matching system for secondary-market trades in government securities.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Primary dealers in the G-Sec market are required to:
o: Underwrite primary auctions and provide two-way quotes
questions.e: Primary dealers underwrite government borrowing auctions and must offer continuous two-way quotes in the secondary market.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The 'held to maturity' (HTM) category of bank investments was capped at what share of NDTL after the 2023 investment norms?
questions.e: The RBI's 2023 investment-portfolio norms capped HTM at 23% of NDTL, with the rest marked under AFS or FVTPL.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Under the RBI's 2021 revised PCA framework, which of these is NOT a trigger parameter?
questions.e: PCA triggers are capital (CRAR), asset quality (net NPAs) and profitability (return on assets); credit-deposit ratio is not a trigger.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Deposit Insurance cover of Rs. 5 lakh applies per depositor:
questions.e: DICGC cover is Rs. 5 lakh per depositor per bank, aggregating all deposits held in the same capacity at that bank.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Interest on savings bank deposits in India is calculated on:
questions.e: Since April 2010, savings interest is computed on the daily closing balance rather than the lowest monthly balance.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) must not have any:
questions.e: BSBDA is a zero-balance no-frills account; banks may cap free withdrawals (e.g., four per month) but cannot demand a minimum balance.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A 'dormant' account in Indian banking terminology is one with no customer-induced transactions for:
questions.e: Accounts with no customer-initiated transactions for two years are classified dormant/inoperative.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Unclaimed deposits transferred to the RBI's DEA Fund relate to accounts inactive for:
questions.e: Balances unclaimed for 10 years or more are transferred to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The UDGAM portal launched by the RBI helps customers:
questions.e: UDGAM (Unclaimed Deposits - Gateway to Access inforMation) centralises search of unclaimed deposits across banks.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Positive Pay, mandated for high-value cheques, requires the issuer to:
o: Share cheque details electronically before clearing
questions.e: Under Positive Pay, issuers of cheques above Rs. 50,000 share key details (date, payee, amount) electronically for cross-verification.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The RBI's 'Sachet' portal is used for:
o: Filing complaints against unregulated deposit-taking entities
questions.e: Sachet lets the public check whether an entity collecting deposits is regulated and file complaints against dubious schemes.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: A bank's 'leverage ratio' under Basel III compares Tier 1 capital to:
questions.e: The leverage ratio is Tier 1 capital divided by total exposure (on- plus off-balance-sheet), with a 3.5% minimum in India.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) in India currently include:
o: SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank
SBI, PNB and Bank of Baroda
questions.e: The RBI's D-SIB list comprises SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, which must hold additional CET1 surcharges of 0.6%, 0.2% and 0.2% respectively.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The additional CET1 surcharge for SBI as a D-SIB is:
questions.e: SBI sits in the highest D-SIB bucket with a 0.6% additional CET1 requirement; HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank carry 0.2%.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Financial Stability Report is published by the RBI:
questions.e: The FSR is released twice a year (June and December), assessing financial-system resilience and macro-financial risks.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The 'Annual Report' of the RBI is addressed to:
questions.e: The RBI's Annual Report is submitted to the Central Government under the RBI Act.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Currency chests are:
o: Select bank branches storing RBI's currency notes
questions.e: Currency chests are select branches of scheduled banks that hold RBI's currency stocks and meet public currency needs.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Select the grammatically correct sentence:
o: Neither of the clerks have submitted the report.
Neither of the clerks has submitted the report.
Neither of the clerks have submit the report.
Neither of the clerks has submit the report.
questions.e: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes 'has submitted'; the present perfect participle 'submitted' is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Identify the error: 'The committee were divided in its opinion on the merger proposal.'
questions.e: When the committee acts as divided individuals, the verb is plural ('were') but the pronoun must be plural too: 'their opinion'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: She has been working in this branch ___ 2019.
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a point of time (2019) in present-perfect-continuous constructions; 'for' needs a duration.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: The manager objected ___ the revised timings.
questions.e: 'Object to' is the correct collocation; 'object against' is not standard English.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'occasion' — double 'c', single 's'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.e: 'Embarrassment' doubles both 'r' and 's'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Synonym of CANDID:
questions.e: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward, synonymous with 'frank'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Synonym of PRUDENT:
questions.e: 'Prudent' means showing care and thought for the future — wise and careful.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Antonym of TRANSPARENT (in the sense of obvious):
questions.e: The opposite of 'transparent' meaning easily seen through is 'obscure' or 'opaque'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Antonym of DILIGENT:
questions.e: 'Diligent' means hard-working; its antonym is 'negligent' (careless, lax).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Idiom: 'to burn the midnight oil' means:
o: To work late into the night
questions.e: 'Burn the midnight oil' means working or studying late into the night.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Idiom: 'once in a blue moon' means:
questions.e: 'Once in a blue moon' describes something that happens very rarely.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Idiom: 'to keep the wolf from the door' means:
o: To have enough money to avoid hunger
questions.e: The idiom means earning enough to keep poverty and hunger away.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One-word substitution: A person who speaks many languages —
questions.e: A polyglot knows or uses several languages; a linguist studies language scientifically.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One-word substitution: Government by a small group of people —
questions.e: 'Oligarchy' is rule by a small elite group.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One-word substitution: An office with no work but high pay —
questions.e: A sinecure is a position requiring little or no work but giving salary or status.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Phrasal verb: 'The merger talks ___ after the due-diligence report.'
questions.e: 'Fall through' means to fail to happen or be completed, as of plans or deals.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Phrasal verb: 'She ___ her old mentor at the banking conclave.'
questions.e: 'Run into' means to meet someone unexpectedly.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: 'He is one of the most brightest students in the batch.'
o: He is one of the most bright students in the batch.
He is one of the brightest students in the batch.
He is one of the more brightest students in the batch.
He is one among the most brightest student in the batch.
questions.e: Double superlatives are wrong: 'one of the' must be followed by the plain superlative 'brightest'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: 'Scarcely had he entered the hall when the lights went off.'
o: Scarcely had he entered the hall than the lights went off.
Scarcely he had entered the hall when the lights went off.
Scarcely did he entered the hall when the lights went off.
questions.e: 'Scarcely/hardly...when' is the correct pairing; the inversion 'had he entered' is already correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank with the right preposition: The new policy is aimed ___ curbing speculative lending.
questions.e: 'Aimed at' is the standard collocation when stating a purpose.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct article usage: '___ RBI is ___ central bank of India.'
questions.e: Unique institutions take 'the': 'The RBI is the central bank of India.'

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Spot the error: 'Each of the candidates were given a token number.'
questions.e: 'Each of' is singular and requires 'was given'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Spot the error: 'He asked me that where I had kept the ledger.'
questions.e: In indirect questions, 'that' is redundant: 'He asked me where I had kept the ledger.'

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word 'IMPECCABLE' is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: 'Impeccable' means without fault or flaw.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word 'MITIGATE' is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: 'Mitigate' means to make less severe — to alleviate.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Arrange in logical order: P. the vault was opened / Q. after the audit team arrived / R. only in the presence of two officers / S. as per protocol
questions.e: The sequence is: after the audit team arrived (Q), the vault was opened (P), only in the presence of two officers (R), as per protocol (S).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Cloze-style: The committee's findings ___ serious lapses in loan appraisal.
questions.e: Findings 'reveal' lapses; the other verbs contradict the sense of an audit report.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Cloze-style: Banks must ___ a balance between growth and risk.
questions.e: The idiomatic collocation is 'strike a balance'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'The auditor flagged the discrepancy.'
o: The discrepancy was flagged by the auditor.
The discrepancy is flagged by the auditor.
The discrepancy has been flagged by the auditor yesterday.
The discrepancy were flagged by the auditor.
questions.e: Simple past active converts to 'was + past participle' in the passive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I will submit the report tomorrow.'
o: He said that he will submit the report tomorrow.
He said that he would submit the report the next day.
He said that he would submit the report tomorrow.
He told that he will submit the report the next day.
questions.e: 'Will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' in reported speech.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Synonym of 'STRINGENT':
questions.e: 'Stringent' means strict, precise and exacting, as of regulations.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Antonym of 'AFFLUENT':
questions.e: 'Affluent' means wealthy; its antonym is 'impoverished'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Idiom: 'to bite the bullet' means:
o: To face a difficult situation bravely
questions.e: To bite the bullet is to endure a painful or unpleasant situation with courage and resolve.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One-word substitution: A remedy for all diseases —
questions.e: A panacea is a cure-all; an antidote counters a specific poison.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: ___ honest officer, he refused the bribe.
questions.e: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Spot the error: 'The data shows that the NPA ratio have declined.'
questions.e: 'Data' used as a singular mass noun here takes singular verbs: 'shows' and 'has declined'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: 'Unless you do not verify the signature, the cheque will be returned.'
o: Unless you verify the signature, the cheque will be returned.
Unless you do not verified the signature, the cheque will be returned.
If you do not verify the signature, the cheque will not be returned.
questions.e: 'Unless' already carries the negative sense, so 'do not' must be dropped.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Phrasal verb: 'The bank decided to ___ with the outdated software.'
questions.e: 'Do away with' means to abolish or discard something.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The cashier was accused of ___ funds.
questions.e: 'Accused of' is followed by a gerund: 'accused of misappropriating funds'.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All clerks are officers. Some officers are managers. Conclusions: I. Some clerks are managers. II. Some managers are clerks.
questions.e: No link connects 'clerks' to 'managers' through the middle term 'officers', so neither conclusion follows.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: No ATM is a branch. All branches are offices. Conclusion: No ATM is an office.
o: Follows only if some offices are branches
questions.e: 'No ATM is a branch' plus 'all branches are offices' validly yields 'no ATM is an office'.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If A > B, B ≥ C and C < D, which of the following is definitely true?
questions.e: From A > B and B ≥ C, A is strictly greater than C. D's relation to A and B is undetermined.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Given P ≤ Q < R = S, which conclusion is definitely false?
questions.e: Q < R = S forces P < S, so 'P = S' can never hold.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, a woman said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman in the photograph related to the speaker?
questions.e: The grandfather's only son is the speaker's father, so his daughter is the speaker's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is B's brother. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.e: A and B are C's children; C is D's daughter, so A is D's grandson.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ravi walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start?
questions.e: The path forms three sides of a rectangle; he ends 3 km east of the starting point.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A man faces east, turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction does he face now?
questions.e: Facing east, a 90° clockwise turn points south; a further 180° anticlockwise turn from south points north.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a code, BANK is written as CBOL. How is LOAN written?
questions.e: Each letter shifts +1: L→M, O→P, A→B, N→O, giving MPBO.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Percentage
capsules.body:
x% of y = (x/100) × y

Successive changes a% and b% combine to a + b + ab/100. Treat a decrease as negative.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Profit & loss
capsules.body:
Profit% = Profit / Cost Price × 100

If marked price is M and discount is d%, selling price = M(1 − d/100). Profit is always compared with cost price.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Simple interest
capsules.body:
SI = P × R × T / 100

Amount under simple interest is P + SI. Keep rate and time in matching annual units.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Compound interest
capsules.body:
A = P(1 + R/100)ᵀ

For half-yearly compounding, halve the annual rate and double the number of periods. CI = A − P.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Average
capsules.body:
Average = Sum of observations / Count

When one value is replaced, change in total = new − old; divide by count for change in average.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Ratio
capsules.body:
a:b = ka:kb

If a total S is divided in m:n, shares are Sm/(m+n) and Sn/(m+n). Ratios compare quantities in the same units.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Time & work
capsules.body:
One-day work = 1 / days required

Add rates when people work together. If A takes a days and B takes b days, together they take ab/(a+b) days.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Pipes & cisterns
capsules.body:
Net rate = inlet rates − outlet rates

Treat filling as positive and emptying as negative; time is reciprocal of the net one-hour work.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Speed, time, distance
capsules.body:
Distance = Speed × Time

Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying 5/18. Relative speed adds in opposite directions and subtracts in the same direction.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Trains
capsules.body:
Time = Total length / Relative speed

For a pole, total length is train length. For a platform, add train and platform lengths. Use metres and m/s.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Boats & streams
capsules.body:
Downstream = boat + stream; upstream = boat − stream

Still-water speed is half the sum; stream speed is half the difference.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Mixture
capsules.body:
Mean price = Total cost / Total quantity

Alligation gives cheaper:dearer quantities = (dearer−mean):(mean−cheaper).

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Data interpretation
capsules.body:
Required value = Read → normalize units → compute

Before calculating, note scale, units, base year and whether the question asks value, difference or percentage change.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Number series
capsules.body:
Check differences, ratios, squares and alternating terms

Do not force a pattern from two gaps; verify it across every available term.

capsules.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
capsules.title: Quadratic equations
capsules.body:
ax² + bx + c = 0

Factor when possible. For comparison questions, find both root sets and compare ranges carefully.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Seating arrangements
capsules.body:
Draw fixed slots before placing people. In a row, facing north means left/right follow the page; facing south reverses them. In a circle, inward-facing left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise; outward-facing reverses that.

  • Place absolute clues first: ends, exact positions, immediate neighbours.
  • Make separate cases only when a clue truly permits alternatives.
  • Use every clue once, then verify every clue at the end.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Syllogism
capsules.body:
Translate statements into set relationships. “All A are B” puts A inside B; it does not mean all B are A. “Some A are B” guarantees an overlap. “No A is B” separates the sets.

  • A universal statement alone does not prove existence.
  • Possibility conclusions ask whether a relation can exist without violating statements.
  • Test conclusions against all valid diagrams, not one convenient drawing.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Inequality
capsules.body:
Join symbols only when the direction is compatible. From A > B ≥ C, conclude A > C. From A > B < C, no definite relation follows between A and C.

  • Equality can pass through ≥ or ≤ chains.
  • For coded inequalities, decode every symbol before solving.
  • A definite conclusion must hold in every value assignment.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Coding–decoding
capsules.body:
Look for letter positions, reversals, shifts, word rearrangement or substitution. In sentence coding, repeated words reveal repeated codes through intersection.

  • Write A=1 to Z=26 when arithmetic is involved.
  • Check whether the rule applies independently to each letter.
  • Never assume the same code type continues across a new question set.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Blood relations
capsules.body:
Create a small family tree with generations on separate levels. Mark gender only when stated. “A is the brother of B” fixes A’s gender, not B’s.

  • Start from the person in the question and work backward.
  • Distinguish maternal and paternal links only when information permits.
  • Spouse relations do not by themselves establish sibling gender.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Direction sense
capsules.body:
Use a coordinate grid: north +y, east +x, south −y, west −x. Final straight-line distance follows √(x²+y²); direction comes from the signs of x and y.

  • Update facing direction after every turn.
  • Right/left are relative to current facing, not the page.
  • Cancel opposite movements before calculating distance.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Ranking & order
capsules.body:
If a person is r-th from the top in a group of n, rank from bottom is n−r+1. If ranks from both ends are given for the same person, total = left rank + right rank − 1.

  • For people between two positions, subtract ranks and then subtract one.
  • Do not combine ranks from different lists without a linking fact.
  • Make a number line for swapping-position problems.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Input–output
capsules.body:
Compare consecutive steps to identify what moves and where. Common rules arrange words alphabetically, numbers ascending/descending, or alternate smallest and largest.

  • Track only the changed element in each step.
  • Confirm the rule on at least two transitions.
  • To find a later step, reproduce the process—not the visible pattern alone.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Data sufficiency
capsules.body:
Judge whether information is enough, not whether you can calculate quickly. Test Statement I alone, Statement II alone, then both together according to the option scheme.

  • Do not import unstated assumptions.
  • A unique value or relation is sufficient.
  • Different exams use different answer-code conventions—read them first.

capsules.subject: Reasoning
capsules.title: Critical reasoning
capsules.body:
An assumption is an unstated bridge required by the argument. A strengthening fact makes the conclusion more likely; a weakening fact attacks the link, evidence or alternative causes.

  • Separate evidence from conclusion.
  • Extreme options are often irrelevant, but reject by logic, not tone.
  • A fact can be true yet fail to address the argument.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Subject–verb agreement
capsules.body:
The verb agrees with the grammatical subject, not the nearest noun. “The quality of the loans is…” Singular indefinite pronouns such as each, either and neither usually take singular verbs.

  • With either…or / neither…nor, agreement usually follows the nearer subject.
  • Amounts treated as one unit take a singular verb.
  • “A number of” is plural; “the number of” is singular.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Tense & sequence
capsules.body:
Use present perfect for an action linked to the present; simple past for a finished time. In reported speech, a past reporting verb often shifts the original tense back, unless the statement remains universally true.

  • Since marks a starting point; for marks a duration.
  • After “did”, use the base verb.
  • Keep a narrative’s time frame consistent.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Articles
capsules.body:
Use “a/an” by sound, not spelling: an hour, a university. Use “the” for something specific, already identified, unique in context, or superlative.

  • Plural and uncountable nouns can appear without an article when general.
  • Job titles after appoint/elect often take no article.
  • Acronyms take a/an based on pronunciation.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Prepositions
capsules.body:
Prepositions express relationships and are learned through usage: responsible for, comply with, differ from, interested in, capable of.

  • Between is standard for distinct individual items; among for a group.
  • Use by for a deadline, until for continuation up to a time.
  • Avoid adding a preposition where the verb does not require one.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Modifiers
capsules.body:
Place a modifier beside the word it describes. A dangling opening phrase has no logical subject: “After reviewing the file, the officer approved it,” not “the approval was given.”

  • Only changes meaning depending on placement.
  • A participial phrase should logically modify the subject that follows.
  • Parallel comparisons must compare like with like.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Parallelism
capsules.body:
Items joined by and/or or listed together should share grammatical form: “to assess, verify and report,” or “assessing, verifying and reporting.”

  • Correlative pairs should join equivalent structures.
  • Do not mix a noun, gerund and clause in one list.
  • Comparison markers such as than should connect comparable forms.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Reading comprehension
capsules.body:
Read for structure: issue, evidence, contrast, author’s stance, conclusion. Answer from the passage, not outside knowledge. For inference, choose what must or most reasonably follows.

  • Broad options overreach; narrow options may miss the main idea.
  • Tone comes from word choice and treatment of opposing views.
  • Return to the exact lines for factual questions.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Cloze test
capsules.body:
Use grammar first, then meaning and collocation. Read the full paragraph before filling blanks so that tone and logical flow guide each choice.

  • Check pronoun reference and tense consistency.
  • Transition words reveal contrast, cause and continuation.
  • Re-read the completed paragraph for coherence.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Para jumbles
capsules.body:
Find an independent opening sentence, then mandatory pairs: pronoun after its noun, example after claim, contrast after position, chronology in order.

  • A sentence beginning with “however” rarely opens the paragraph.
  • Repeated keywords and synonyms create links.
  • Confirm the final order as one coherent argument.

capsules.subject: English
capsules.title: Vocabulary in context
capsules.body:
Meaning depends on the sentence. Replace the word with each option and check both dictionary sense and tone. Learn word families and common collocations, not isolated lists.

  • Use roots and affixes as clues, not proof.
  • A synonym may have the wrong register or preposition.
  • Record new words with one original sentence.

capsules.subject: RBI
capsules.title: RBI's October 2026 liquidity tightening (9–13 Oct)
capsules.body: The RBI raised minimum daily CRR maintenance from 90% to 99% of the requirement (effective from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026), announced a Rs 25,000-crore OMO bond sale on 13 October 2026, barred rebooking of cancelled rupee derivative contracts, cut the no-underlying-exposure FX threshold to $5 million, introduced a 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve for contracts above $2 million, and opened a special dollar window for three public-sector oil marketing companies — all to drain surplus liquidity and defend the rupee.

capsules.subject: RBI Policy
capsules.title: RBI MPC Oct 2026: repo 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%), calibrated tightening
capsules.body: The RBI’s MPC (5–7 October 2026) unanimously hiked the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% — the first increase since February 2023, reversing part of the 125-bps cuts of 2025. Vide circular RBI/2026-27/282 dated 7 October 2026, the SDF rate is 5.25% and the MSF rate and Bank Rate 5.75%, effective immediately. The stance moved from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ (4–2 majority) — rate cuts are off the table. Governor Sanjay Malhotra blamed the September re-escalation of the West Asia conflict, crude near USD 100/barrel, deficient monsoon and food/fuel/fertiliser pressures. FY27 projections: real GDP 7.1% (up from 6.7%), CPI 5.2%; August CPI was 4.82%.

capsules.subject: RBI Policy
capsules.title: MPC voting and stance: unanimous hike, 4–2 for calibrated tightening (7 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The six-member MPC’s rate-hike decision on 7 October 2026 was unanimous, while the stance change to ‘calibrated tightening’ passed 4–2. Context: in August 2026 the panel had held the repo at 5.25% with a neutral stance (also unanimous). This is the first rate-increase cycle since February 2023, when the repo was raised to 6.50%. For banking aspirants: ‘calibrated tightening’ means the RBI will either hike or pause going ahead — an easing bias is ruled out until inflation durably returns toward the 4% target.

capsules.subject: RBI
capsules.title: RBI's October forex package: hedging-only NDDCs, 20% risk reserve (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: In a circular on 12 October 2026, the RBI amended the Master Direction on Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings: authorised dealers may offer INR non-deliverable derivative contracts to non-residents only for hedging; a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve applies to certain AD transactions; rules on rebooking cancelled contracts were tightened. The package followed a slide in the rupee, which closed at 95.78/$ on 12 October before firming to 95.05 early on 13 October.

capsules.subject: RBI
capsules.title: Liquidity tightening: daily CRR 99% and Rs 25,000-cr OMO sale (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: After the 25-bps repo hike to 5.50%, the RBI raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance to 99% (from 90%) effective the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026 — the first such move since July 2013 — and sold Rs 25,000 crore of government securities on 13 October to align overnight rates with the repo rate.

capsules.subject: Monetary Policy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026 policy: repo at 5.50%, stance turns to calibrated tightening
capsules.body: On 7 October 2026 the six-member MPC unanimously hiked the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% (first hike since February 2023). The Standing Deposit Facility rate is 5.25%, and the Marginal Standing Facility rate and Bank Rate are 5.75%. The stance moved from neutral to calibrated tightening on a 4–2 vote, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra noting rate cuts are off the table in the near term.

capsules.subject: Monetary Policy
capsules.title: RBI’s growth and inflation outlook: FY27 GDP at 7.1%, CPI at 5.2%
capsules.body: The RBI raised its FY2026–27 real GDP growth forecast from 6.7% to 7.1% while lifting projected CPI inflation to 5.2%, after headline inflation rose to 4.8% in August 2026 and the economy grew 7.8% in Q1. The next MPC meeting is scheduled for 2–4 December 2026.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI to enable interoperability among NBFC Account Aggregators
capsules.body: In the October 2026 policy, the RBI announced it will facilitate interoperability among NBFC-Account Aggregators, letting customers access and share financial information across financial service providers through any account aggregator of their choice. SEBI-regulated depositories will also include bank deposit account information in the consolidated account statement (CAS).

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: IDBI Bank–Fairfax deal: ₹52,878 crore, largest FDI in Indian finance
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet’s 14 October 2026 approval of the IDBI Bank sale to Fairfax at ₹52,878 crore is the largest-ever foreign direct investment in India’s financial sector. Post-deal, the government’s stake falls to 15% and LIC’s to 19%.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: IBPS Clerk (CRP CSA-XVI) Prelims held 10-11 Oct 2026
capsules.body: IBPS conducted the Clerk (Customer Service Associate) Prelims 2026 under CRP CSA-XVI on 10 and 11 October 2026 for 11,663 posts. The prelims carried 100 marks over 60 minutes (English Language, Numerical Ability, Reasoning Ability) with 1/4 negative marking; the paper was rated easy-to-moderate across shifts. The Mains is scheduled for 27 December 2026.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: UIIC AO 2026: admit card on 15 Oct, prelims on 22 Oct
capsules.body: United India Insurance Company will release the UIIC AO Admit Card 2026 on 15 October 2026 for the Administrative Officer (Scale-I) prelims scheduled on 22 October 2026. The drive covers 225 vacancies (Generalists and Hindi Officer).

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI MPC (5–7 Oct 2026): repo hiked to 5.50%, stance to calibrated tightening
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee met 5–7 October 2026 under Governor Sanjay Malhotra and unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% — the first hike in nearly three years — changing the stance from neutral to 'calibrated tightening'. SDF is 5.25% and MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%; FY27 GDP growth is projected at 7.1% and CPI inflation at 5.2%.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI tightens daily CRR maintenance to 99% from 16 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The RBI raised the minimum daily maintenance of the prescribed CRR from 90% to 99% effective 16 October 2026 (the overall CRR stays at 3%), alongside an open market sale of government securities worth ₹25,000 crore to absorb excess liquidity. The move aims to bring short-term borrowing rates closer to the repo rate and improve monetary-policy transmission.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: SC quashes Yes Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT1 bond write-off (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: A Supreme Court Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih on 15 October 2026 upheld the Bombay High Court's 20 January 2023 judgment quashing Yes Bank's write-off of ₹8,415 crore of Additional Tier 1 bonds during its March 2020 restructuring (Yes Bank v Axis Trusteeship). The RBI had placed Yes Bank under moratorium on 5 March 2020 and formulated a reconstruction scheme under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI forex circular (12 Oct 2026): no-underlying derivative threshold cut to $5M
capsules.body: Under A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 27 dated 12 October 2026, the RBI reduced the threshold for specified forex derivative transactions without establishing underlying exposure from US$100 million to US$5 million, restricted Authorised Dealers to offering INR-involving NDDCs to non-residents only for hedging, and introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve of 20% of the INR-equivalent notional, to be held in cash with the RBI daily.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: NABARD hires 16 cyber-security specialists on contract — apply 9–26 Oct 2026 (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: NABARD (Advt No. 04/2026-27) is hiring 16 specialists on contract for CISO & DoS-CSITE at Head Office, Mumbai: SOC Analyst (3), Information Security Analyst (3), Network Security Analyst (1), Ethical Hacker & Penetration Tester (1), Lead Auditor (2), Cyber & Network Security Specialist (2), IT Banking Specialist (2), Cyber Security Analyst (2). Apply 9–26 October 2026 at nabard.org; remuneration ₹12–40 lakh p.a. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: Canara Bank: 3,500 Graduate Apprentice seats — last date 17 Oct 2026 (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Canara Bank's FY 2026-27 notification covers 3,500 Graduate Apprentice seats across states/UTs (Karnataka 581, UP 409, Tamil Nadu 391 largest). Eligibility: 20–28 years, graduation between 1 Jan 2023 and 1 Sep 2026, 60% in Class 12/Diploma (55% SC/ST/PwBD). Selection by state-wise merit; stipend ₹16,650/month. Apply 1–17 October 2026 at canarabank.bank.in after 100%-complete NATS registration. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Banking awareness
capsules.title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%; 'calibrated tightening' (7 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The RBI's MPC, at its 63rd meeting chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, unanimously raised the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — and shifted the stance to 'calibrated tightening' (supported 4-2). SDF at 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate at 5.75%, CRR 3.00%, SLR 18.00%. FY27 GDP growth projected at 7.1%, CPI inflation at 5.2%.

capsules.subject: Banking awareness
capsules.title: SC dismisses Yes Bank AT-1 bond appeals (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih dismissed appeals in Yes Bank Ltd. & Anr. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd. & Ors. (2026 INSC 1132), leaving the Bombay High Court's decision — which set aside the Rs. 8,415 crore write-down of AT-1 bonds — undisturbed. The judgment examines whether an administrator can exercise a write-down power that the governing legal framework assigns to the RBI.

capsules.subject: Banking awareness
capsules.title: Cabinet approves IDBI Bank stake sale to Fairfax (14 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet approved the sale of a stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax for Rs. 52,878 crore on 14 October 2026 — one of the largest recent disinvestment-related transactions in the banking sector.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: RBI approves Emirates NBD India branches–RBL Bank merger — Verified: 17 Oct 2026
capsules.body: On 16 October 2026 the RBI approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of the Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. with RBL Bank, effective 1 December 2026. This followed Emirates NBD's acquisition of a 60% stake in RBL Bank via a Rs 26,000 crore primary capital infusion in June 2026 — the largest foreign direct investment in the Indian banking sector.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: IBPS/RRB calendar: what remains in 2026–27 — Verified: 17 Oct 2026
capsules.body: Upcoming banking exams for the 2026–27 cycle: IBPS SO Main on 1 November 2026; RRB Officer Scale-I Prelims on 21–22 November and Main on 20 December 2026; RRB Office Assistant Prelims on 6, 12 and 13 December and Main on 30 January 2027; RRB Scale II & III single exam on 20 December 2026.

capsules.title: IBPS 2026-27: remaining exam dates for Clerk, SO and RRB
capsules.body: The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection's tentative calendar 2026-27 (ibps.in) lists the key upcoming dates: IBPS Clerk (CSA) prelims 10–11 October 2026, mains 27 December 2026; SO mains 1 November 2026; RRB Officer Scale I prelims 21–22 November, mains 20 December 2026; RRB Office Assistant prelims 6, 12 & 13 December, mains 30 January 2027; RRB Officer Scale II & III single exam on 20 December 2026. SBI Clerk mains are tentatively set for 23 November 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI approves Emirates NBD–RBL Bank merger from 1 Dec 2026
capsules.body: The Reserve Bank of India has approved the amalgamation of the Indian branches of Dubai-based Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. with RBL Bank, effective 1 December 2026, from which date the Indian branches operate as RBL Bank branches. The approval follows Emirates NBD's acquisition of a 60% stake in RBL Bank's expanded share capital on 18 June 2026 for about ₹26,016 crore (92.91 crore shares at ₹280 each); the Finance Ministry had earlier cleared a proposal to acquire up to 74%.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Forex reserves $726.03 bn (9 Oct); rupee rebounds to 94.71
capsules.body: India's forex reserves fell USD 8.578 billion in the week ended 9 October 2026 to USD 726.03 billion (RBI), down roughly USD 60 billion over six weeks from the 4 September peak of USD 785.7 billion as RBI sold dollars to defend the rupee. The rupee meanwhile posted its biggest weekly gain in seven months, closing at ₹94.71 per dollar on 16 October. Bank credit grew 19.4% YoY and deposits 17.8% YoY (30 September 2026), and the WTO raised its 2026 merchandise trade growth forecast to 3.9%.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI MPC 7 October 2026: repo 5.50%, calibrated tightening
capsules.body: The MPC voted unanimously to raise the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — and shifted the stance to 'calibrated tightening' (4–2). Corridor: SDF 5.25%, repo 5.50%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. FY27: GDP 7.1%, CPI 5.2%. Rate cuts are off the table for now; the next move is a hike or a pause.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: Yes Bank AT-1: Supreme Court sets aside Rs 8,415 crore write-down
capsules.body: On 15 October 2026 (2026 INSC 1132), the Supreme Court dismissed appeals by Yes Bank, the RBI and the Union government against the Bombay High Court's order setting aside the write-down of Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore. Key principle: the write-down could not survive once the final Reconstruction Scheme omitted a write-down provision — administrative action must stay within the statute, regulations and the final scheme.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: SCL Das to head FSIB for three years
capsules.body: The Centre appointed Subhas Chandra Lal Das as part-time chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) for three years on 17 October 2026, along with former bankers and RBI officials. FSIB recommends board-level appointments at public sector banks and financial institutions.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: FY27 outlook: 7.1% GDP, 5.2% CPI
capsules.body: The RBI's October 2026 policy projects 7.1% real GDP growth for FY27 (Q2: 7.2%, Q3: 6.9%, Q4: 6.8%) and 5.2% CPI inflation (Q2: 4.9%, Q3: 6.0%, Q4: 5.7%). August 2026 CPI was 4.8%, driven by food and fuel, with core inflation broadening.

capsules.title: JAIIB November 2026: paper-wise dates
capsules.body: IIBF's JAIIB November 2026 cycle: IE & IFS — 1 November, PPB — 22 November, AFM — 28 November, RBWM — 29 November 2026. Each paper: 100 MCQs, 2 hours, 100 marks, no negative marking; pass mark 50.

capsules.subject: Bank Exams
capsules.title: IBPS SO Prelims result 2026 out; Mains on 1 November
capsules.body: The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection declared the Specialist Officers Preliminary Examination Result 2026 on 15 October 2026 for the CRP SPL-XVI cycle. The drive aims to fill 1,043 vacancies across six streams — IT Officer, Agricultural Field Officer, Law Officer, Rajbhasha Adhikari, HR/Personnel Officer and Marketing Officer. capsules.body: IBPS has raised the indicative vacancies for its Customer Service Associate (clerk) recruitment CRP CSA-XVI from 11,403 to 11,663 through a corrigendum dated 29 September 2026, covering 11 banks across 37 states and UTs (Union Bank of India figures still not reported). capsules.body: SBI released the Probationary Officers Prelims 2026 answer key on 12 October 2026 on the SBI Careers portal for 1,500 PO vacancies under Advt. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09 (exam held 1-2 August 2026). Candidates can log in with their registration number and date of birth to view their response sheets; SBI's answer-key policy is final and not challengeable. Qualified candidates now prepare for the Mains and the Group Exercise plus Interview round.

capsules.title: Upcoming banking exams: RRB PO, RRB Clerk, Clerk and SBI Clerk Mains
capsules.body: The remaining 2026 banking examination calendar: IBPS SO Mains on 1 November; SBI Clerk Mains on 23 November (tentative); IBPS RRB PO Prelims on 21-22 November and Mains on 20 December; IBPS RRB Clerk Prelims on 6, 12 and 13 December; IBPS Clerk (CSA-XVI) Mains on 27 December; and IBPS RRB Clerk Mains on 30 January 2027. Candidates should verify dates on ibps.in and SBI Careers.

capsules.subject: RBI
capsules.title: RBI October 2026 policy: every key rate in one place
capsules.body: The MPC's 63rd meeting (5-7 October 2026) under Governor Sanjay Malhotra: repo rate 5.25% to 5.50% (+25 bps, first hike since February 2023, unanimous vote); SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; CRR 3.00%; SLR 18.00%. Stance: 'calibrated tightening' (4-2 vote; Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh wanted 'neutral') - rate cuts are off the table; the next move can only be a hike or a pause. The RBI expects headline CPI to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters, and projects 5.2% CPI and 7.1% real GDP growth for FY27. Forex reserves cover about 11 months of imports. The RBI also announced NBFC account aggregators will be made interoperable and a technical consultative committee on financial markets will be set up.

capsules.subject: Banking
capsules.title: RBI's special dollar window for oil marketing companies (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Among the October 2026 measures credited by ASSOCHAM with helping the rupee recover nearly 2% from its lows: the RBI opened a special dollar window for public-sector oil marketing companies, set up a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve, tightened foreign exchange derivative norms, conducted open market operations and raised the cash reserve ratio requirement. The special window shifts an estimated $11-12 billion of monthly dollar demand from oil companies away from the spot market, easing pressure on the rupee amid crude oil costs of $114-116 per barrel.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: SBI PO Mains 2026 result: 4,367 qualify for Phase 3
capsules.body: The State Bank of India declared the Probationary Officer Mains 2026 result on 15 October 2026 for 1,500 posts (Advt No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09); the Mains was held on 12 September 2026. 4,367 candidates have qualified for Phase 3, published as a roll-number PDF on sbi.bank.in (no login needed). Phase 3: psychometric test tentatively on 31 October 2026, followed by group exercises and interviews from 18 November 2026. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

capsules.subject: Financial Inclusion
capsules.title: Financial inclusion saturation campaign: 21 Oct - 31 Dec 2026
capsules.body: The Finance Ministry will run a nationwide financial inclusion saturation campaign from 21 October to 31 December 2026, covering 2.70 lakh gram panchayats and urban local bodies. Banks will conduct camps for enrolments, Aadhaar seeding under PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana, besides updating nominations in savings accounts and other facilities. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: RBI MPC (7 Oct 2026): repo raised 25 bps to 5.50%; stance to 'calibrated tightening'
capsules.body: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (meeting 5-7 October 2026, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra) voted unanimously to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — and shifted the stance from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening'. The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate moved to 5.25%; the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and Bank Rate to 5.75%. The Governor noted inflation and its outlook were 'not benign as they were last year'. Context: August CPI inflation 4.82% (up from 4.45% in July), crude above $100/barrel, rupee ~96.36/USD, FY27 inflation forecast raised to 5.2%, Q1 FY27 real GDP growth 7.8%. The stance change signals rate cuts are off the table near-term; ahead lies only another hike or a pause. Two MPC members (Dr Nagesh Kumar, Prof Ram Singh) favoured retaining a neutral stance even as the rate vote was unanimous.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: RBI raises minimum daily CRR maintenance to 99% (w.e.f. 16 Oct 2026 fortnight)
capsules.body: The RBI has raised the minimum daily Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for scheduled banks from 90% to 99%, effective from the reporting fortnight beginning 16 October 2026 (notification dated 9 Oct 2026, signed by Manoranjan Padhy, CGM, Department of Regulation, under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934). Banks must now keep at least 99% of the prescribed CRR on each day of the fortnight, though average compliance over the fortnight still applies. The prescribed CRR rate itself is unchanged at 3%. Rationale: drain/manage surplus liquidity (surplus ~Rs 4 lakh crore; average LAF surplus Rs 5.9 lakh crore since August) as the RBI shifts to calibrated tightening. Effect: banks lose operational flexibility in daily reserve management (they can no longer run at 90% for part of the fortnight and compensate later); short-term funding costs may firm up.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 in force from 1 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The RBI has notified the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which came into force on 1 October 2026. Key provisions: AD banks must upload export/import data in EDPMS/IDPMS within 5 working days for non-EDI ports; timeline for realisation and repatriation of export proceeds is 15 months (extended to 18 months for exports invoiced or settled in Indian rupees); self-declaration allowed for closure of export-monitoring entries up to Rs 10 lakh.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: RBI proposes doubling UCB unsecured-advances ceiling to 20%; Mission-SAKSHAM
capsules.body: The RBI has proposed doubling the aggregate ceiling on unsecured advances for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) from 10% to 20% of total assets, with implementation scheduled from 1 October 2026. Fine print: additional unsecured advances beyond the ceiling allowed only for priority-sector-eligible loans up to Rs 50,000 per borrower; lending limit to nominal members for consumer durables proposed at Rs 2.5 lakh per borrower; maximum unsecured loan limits of Rs 5 lakh (Tier-1), Rs 7.5 lakh (Tier-2) and Rs 10 lakh (Tier-3/4); tenor and moratorium for housing loans deregulated for Tier-3 and Tier-4 UCBs. The RBI also announced Mission-SAKSHAM to train over 1.4 lakh UCB staff in governance, technology and risk management. Regulator of UCBs: RBI; there are over 1,500 UCBs.

capsules.subject: Banking Awareness
capsules.title: Policy signal: rate cuts off the table; up to 75 bps more tightening possible
capsules.body: The October 2026 policy marks a directional change, not a one-off: after a cumulative 125 bps of cuts in 2025 and a four-meeting pause at 5.25%, the MPC's 'calibrated tightening' stance means rate cuts are off the table near-term — future action can only be a hike or a pause. Economists see scope for up to 75 bps of cumulative tightening, with the repo potentially near 6% by end-FY27, depending on inflation, oil and global conditions.

capsules.subject: Banking awareness
capsules.title: India to release AI regulation consultation paper within a month (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: 21 Oct 2026. Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced on 8 October 2026 that MeitY will release a consultation paper on AI regulation within a month, forming the base of India's future AI regulatory framework. Key focus: AI safety (called 'the most important point'), human-centric development, skilling, and emerging risks including deepfakes, cybersecurity threats and psychological harms. The government will follow a techno-legal approach, with industry stakeholders taking primary responsibility for user safety. Exam angle: regulatory-awareness questions on India's digital policy and the IndiaAI Mission.

capsules.subject: Monetary Policy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026: repo 5.50%, calibrated tightening (minutes 21 Oct)
capsules.body:
RBI's October 2026 policy (minutes released 21 Oct): repo raised 25 bps to 5.50% — first hike since Feb 2023 — with SDF at 5.25% and MSF/Bank Rate at 5.75%. The MPC voted 4–2 to move the stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening,” taking rate cuts off the table; the next move is a hike or a pause. Governor: Sanjay Malhotra.

Context: CPI at 4.8% in August (third month above the 4% target), crude $114–116/barrel, 13% monsoon deficit. FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1%. Next MPC: 2–4 Dec 2026.

capsules.subject: Financial Markets
capsules.title: Goldman Sachs: India's listed AI market could gain $50–100 bn via IPOs
capsules.body:
A Goldman Sachs report (21 Oct 2026) says India's listed AI market could gain $50–100 billion in market capitalisation over the next 2–5 years as private AI companies list. It identified 84 privately held Indian AI firms worth ~$55 billion (71 at growth/late/infrastructure/buyout stages worth ~$54 bn); 25–50% could IPO at ~4x valuations.

PE funding for Indian AI startups has tripled since 2024; AI now accounts for about one-fifth of all private capital invested in India — a top-six global destination for private AI funding.

capsules.title: LIC HFL Apprenticeship Program-010: 232 seats, apply by 1 Nov
capsules.body:
LIC Housing Finance notified its Apprenticeship Program-010 on 20 Oct 2026: 232 apprentice seats across 25 states/UTs (Maharashtra 28, Tamil Nadu 29, Karnataka 24...). Apply 20 Oct–1 Nov 2026 on nats.education.gov.in.

capsules.subject: Personal Finance
capsules.title: Small-savings rates unchanged for Q3 FY27; DICGC cover ₹5 lakh
capsules.body:
The Finance Ministry has kept small-savings rates unchanged for Oct–Dec 2026: PPF 7.1%, Senior Citizens Savings Scheme 8.2%. Bank deposits remain insured by DICGC up to ₹5,00,000 (principal + interest).

Floating-rate loans linked to the repo rate will reset higher at the next EMI revision after the 25-bps hike — e.g. ~₹469/month more on a ₹30L, 20-year home loan at 8% with full pass-through.

capsules.subject: Technology
capsules.title: JEET AI launches India's first AI tutor at ₹1,499/month (21 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
JEET AI (by Extramarks Education, founder Ritvik Kulshrestha) launched on 21 Oct 2026 as India's first AI tutor that actively teaches — writing on a virtual board, using simulations, and pausing to test comprehension — rather than just answering questions.

Launched in Hindi (Tamil, Kannada next), at ₹1,499/month. Banking relevance: AI-led personalised learning models are reshaping ed-fintech and skilling economics.

capsules.subject: RBI
capsules.title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50% — first hike in nearly four years
capsules.body: The RBI's six-member MPC unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% at its 5–7 October 2026 meeting and adopted a 'calibrated tightening' stance. Minutes released 21 October 2026 note that 37% of CPI-basket items had inflation above 4% in August (vs 20% in March), GDP growth for FY2026-27 is now forecast at 7.1%, and headline CPI may touch 6% in Q3. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)
